Moreover, the moral imperative to eradicate societal ills like criminality or intellectual stagnation outweighs ethical qualms about coercion. Let us courageously pursue this vision, for the legacy we bequeath to future generations is not merely their environment but their very essence. In the pursuit of a perfected world, we must dare to redefine what it means to be human.

In the late 19th century, biologist August Weismann conducted experiments (such as cutting off the tails of mice for several generations) to test Lamarckism. He found that the offspring continued to be born with full-length tails. This led to the concept of the Weismann Barrier, a principle stating that hereditary information moves only from genes to body cells, and never from body cells to genes. This barrier effectively disproved the central mechanism of Lamarckism.

While strict Lamarckism is rejected, modern biology has discovered epigenetics. Epigenetics involves changes in gene expression (whether a gene is turned on or off) rather than changes in the genetic code itself.
